message.content:
Here are some of the most popular and widely read books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Title | Year Published | Notes |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (titled *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | First book in the Harry Potter series; introduces Hogwarts, the wizarding world, and the main characters. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Second installment; explores the mystery of the Chamber and the basilisk. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Third book; introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Fourth book; features the Triwizard Tournament and the return of Voldemort. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Fifth book; focuses on Dumbledore’s Army and the Ministry’s interference. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince** | 2005 | Sixth book; delves into Voldemort’s backstory and Horcruxes. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Final book; concludes the epic saga with the Battle of Hogwarts. |
| **Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them** | 2001 (book) / 2016 (film) | Companion guide to magical creatures; later expanded into a film series. |
| **Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald** | 2018 | Sequel to the first film; continues the story of Newt Scamander. |
| **Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore** | 2022 | Latest installment in the film series. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel; a political drama set in a small English town. |
| **The Cuckoo’s Calling** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013 | Debut crime novel under her pseudonym; follows private investigator Cormoran Strike. |
| **The Silkworm** | 2014 | Second book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Career of Evil** | 2015 | Third book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Lethal White** | 2018 | Fourth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |

These titles cover the core Harry Potter series, the expanded Fantastic Beasts universe, and Rowling’s ventures into adult fiction both under her own name and her pseudonym.
